Summary (full text)

Camera wyze-t20x-jxf23 (T20) in the light box with the SpyderCheckr 24 chart, lamps 5000 K. Both stacks ran on the same camera, the same chart position and the same light: the open stack (open-tx-isp + OpenIMP + streamer) and the vendor stack (Ingenic ISP module + vendor libimp + streamer built for it), one after the other.

Result: 78 pass, 6 fail (4 issues, 2 open), 120 info/warn, 1 beyond vendor (documented), 2 planned checks not run in these runs.

Failed checks: NV12 Y temporal std / mean Y at gain 2 (%) (open 1.135, vendor 1.004; pass = open <= vendor x 1.1 (noise relative to the picture level)); NV12 Y temporal std / mean Y at gain 4 (%) (open 2.019, vendor 1.413; pass = open <= vendor x 1.1 (noise relative to the picture level)); cmp: AEC modulated noise: ERLE >= 10 dB (or vendor - 3 dB), residual <= 3 dB (open ERLE 50.5, residual 20.1 dB, vendor ERLE 52.9, residual 17.5 dB; b91 rule; reference); cmp: AEC speech-like: ERLE >= 10 dB (or vendor - 3 dB), residual <= 3 dB (open ERLE 52.9, residual 3.7 dB, vendor ERLE 52.8, residual 3.7 dB; b91 rule; reference); time to stable AE: ae_compensation 64 (s) (open 14, vendor 10; 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; vendor-relative rule: open worse than vendor by > 10 % = warn, > 25 % = fail; here open is 40 % worse than the vendor); time to stable AE: ssim: after restart (ref 12000 kbps) (s) (open 12, vendor 9; 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; vendor-relative rule: open worse than vendor by > 10 % = warn, > 25 % = fail; here open is 33 % worse than the vendor).

Warnings: time to stable AE: enc h264 fixqp35: after restart (s) (open 12, vendor 10): 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; vendor-relative rule: open worse than vendor by > 10 % = warn, > 25 % = fail; here open is 20 % worse than the vendor; time to stable AE: noisecurve: manual IT/gain 4 (s) (open 12, vendor 10): 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; vendor-relative rule: open worse than vendor by > 10 % = warn, > 25 % = fail; here open is 20 % worse than the vendor; time to stable AE: noisecurve: manual IT/gain max (s) (open 12, vendor 10): 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; 3 exposure reads 2 s apart within 2 %; vendor-relative rule: open worse than vendor by > 10 % = warn, > 25 % = fail; here open is 20 % worse than the vendor; picture check before cpu (open - , vendor monochrome with the lamps on ): advisory (Claude vision, lamps_on); see vision/cpu.json.

Passed: frame luma p1_day (AE target, default comp 128); frame luma p1_night (AE target, default comp 128); chart grey RG (AWB, unclipped grey patches, 1.0 = neutral); chart grey BG (AWB, unclipped grey patches, 1.0 = neutral); p1_day dE00 mean, unclipped patches; p1_day dE00 mean, grey-normalised; grey row tone slope; MTF50 median of the common chart edges (cycles/pixel); 10-90 % edge rise median of the common edges (px); H.264 FixQP 25: decodes clean; ...

How to read: "pass" means the open stack is equal to or better than the vendor stack within the tolerance named in each row; matched-exposure rows (A2) compare the same integration time and gain on both stacks, read back from the ISP.

Method

  • Same camera, same chart position, same lamps; open stack first, then the vendor ISP module + vendor libimp are loaded from /tmp (nothing flashed); the camera returns to the flashed image at the end (module reload or reboot).
  • P1 = camera defaults (AE, AWB, comp 128). P2 = matched exposure: the same integration time and gains on both stacks, set inside the streamer and read back from the ISP; rows whose read-back differs are marked verify=FAIL and not compared.
  • A/A: point p2_a is measured twice (p2_a, p2_a2); the relative difference is the repeatability of the method. A difference between the stacks counts only beyond 2 x that spread (floor 5 %).
  • NV12 noise is measured on raw NV12 frames from the streamer (no JPEG in the path): temporal standard deviation per pixel over the burst, mean over Y 32..224, and U/V.
  • Colour: SpyderCheckr 24 detected automatically, sRGB -> Lab (D50), CIEDE2000 against the Datacolor default values (D50 assumed, not batch specific); 'grey-normalised' removes the white-balance cast first.
  • Sharpness: slanted-edge method on the chart's outer patch edges, frames averaged against noise; JPEG snapshot path.
  • SSIM/PSNR (when run): both stacks record the same static chart scene at the same bitrate; each stream is decoded and compared against a high-bitrate capture of the SAME stack (reference), so the number is the encoder loss of that stack; a cross-stack comparison on static frames is listed separately and includes the ISP difference.
  • Encoder (A5): both stacks get the same streamer settings (codec, rc_mode, qp / bitrate, gop) through a /tmp conf and a streamer restart; the recordings come over RTSP (ffmpeg -c copy). The reference is a mean image, because single NV12 frames are not frame-aligned with the stream; the scene is static, so every decoded frame can be compared with it. A second reference at the end of the phase shows whether the scene or the AE moved in between.
  • Lamp switches are made by a person on a marker (NEED_* file); the times above are the marker times.
